Package com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client

Class GooglyTracker

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.client.GooglyTracker
public class GooglyTracker extends Object
Per-entity client-side eye state: the GooglyTracker.EyeInfo pupil-physics simulator for every configured eye, plus which BehaviorInstance (if any) is currently playing on that entity.

One tracker is kept per tracked LivingEntity (see ClientEyeRuntime), matched against the entity's current placement via matches(com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.HeadInfo). update(com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.BehaviorSettings) advances the active behavior and steps every eye's physics once per client tick; startBehavior(com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.eye.behavior.EyeBehavior, int, long, int) applies a server-triggered behavior, enforcing the "one at a time, non-interruptable" rule.

Each tick also folds in the OngoingBehaviors whose server switches are on, easing each one in or out over a few ticks: the sleeping squint, or a sleeping villager's lids closing to a slit; the ramming goat's squint; the archer's one-eyed aim, closing the eye away from the arm holding the weapon; the swelling creeper's rattle, kicking its pupils back into flight in proportion to the swell; red pupils for an attacking mob or one the server reports angry; and the creepy enderman's pupil pulse, at a frequency of its own. None of these blocks a behavior: each sits on top of whatever plays. A sleeping entity starts no new behavior whether or not its squint is on.

    • GooglyTracker

      public GooglyTracker(@Nonnull net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity parent, @Nonnull HeadInfo helper, boolean angry, @Nonnull BehaviorSettings settings)
      Build the tracker. angry is the server-reported anger already known for this entity, so a tracker built for an angry mob starts red, as one built for a sleeping mob starts squinted or lidded; settings says which ongoing behaviors are on.

    • startBehavior

      public boolean startBehavior(@Nonnull EyeBehavior behavior, int duration, long seed, int elapsed)
      Start a behavior now, unless one is already playing — the "one at a time, non-interruptable" rule — or the entity is asleep. Returns whether it started (a dropped trigger returns false). Called from the trigger packet on the client.

      elapsed starts the behavior that many ticks in, so a player who starts watching a mob mid-effect sees the same state as everyone else: the seeded onStart plus the age fully determine each behavior's influence.

    • update

      public void update(BehaviorSettings settings)
      Advance one client tick: sample the entity's motion, age the active behavior, and step every eye, with the ongoing behaviors settings switches on folded in.
